bullets.body: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) closed Wednesday at $224.85, up 3.6 percent from Tuesday's $217.05 print and lifting the stock to a fresh all-time intraday high of $228.40 inside the cash session, on volume of approximately 21.4 million shares — the sixth-highest volume session of the post-IPO record. The state-change driving the tape was a Wednesday pre-market initiation from Goldman Sachs analyst Toshiya Hari at Buy with a $260 twelve-month target — the first formal Goldman coverage initiation on Cerebras since the IPO — alongside a Citi initiation at Buy with a $245 target, both citing the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close as the catalyst that resolves the customer-concentration overhang flagged in the S-1. Bloomberg reported that the Wednesday tape also crossed an options-flow milestone: the open-interest tally on the September 2026 $240 call line lifted past 92,400 contracts, the first six-figure-equivalent build on any single CBRS strike since the post-Alphabet analyst-day Friday, and the Cboe weekly straddle pricing implied a forward 30-day realized-volatility band of 58 percent against the prior 71 percent. Reuters separately confirmed that institutional buyside cumulative net position lifted to approximately 49.8 percent of float on Wednesday tape from Tuesday's 47.5 percent.

bullets.body: Anthropic published a Wednesday security advisory disclosing CVE-2026-46198, a high-severity (CVSS 8.7) variant of the prior-Tuesday Codex CLI prompt-injection-escalation pattern, this time landing in Claude Code 3.0's MCP-server tool-call deserialization path on the dev branch v3.0.14-rc2 — the same JSON-Schema validation gap class that Trail of Bits Vasilios Mavroudis and Pillar Security Dor Sarig surfaced in the OpenAI Codex CLI on 5/26, found here by Anthropic's internal red team after they reviewed the GitHub Security Lab advisory and audited Claude Code's analogous tool-call path. Anthropic shipped a patched v3.0.14 stable tag inside the same Wednesday window adding the same strict schema validation plus runtime tool-call audit log primitive that OpenAI shipped on Tuesday, and Anthropic's note states that the Claude Code 3.0 production-tier auto-update path will force-roll all v3.0.13-and-earlier tenants to v3.0.14 inside 48 hours. The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog placed CVE-2026-46198 on the KEV list Wednesday afternoon after Mandiant confirmed a second Fortune 500 incident-response engagement — this time at a Fortune 500 healthcare customer — and the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy now stands at thirteen catalogued instances. Sysdig separately published a Wednesday threat-intel note observing that the median credential-extraction time-to-first-exploit on unprotected Claude Code 3.0 estates with v3.0.13-or-earlier installed dropped to 3 minutes 40 seconds from the prior Codex CLI baseline of 5 minutes.

bullets.body: The vLLM project shipped its v0.11.5 development branch cut to a release candidate tag v0.11.5-rc1 on Wednesday afternoon Pacific time, the first development-branch release-candidate since v0.11.4 went stable on May 18 and the first vLLM RC to ship native Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B Mixture-of-Experts kernel support with the expert-fused-router pass that Tianle Cai and Woosuk Kwon first prototyped in the May 12 vLLM project-meeting notes. The release-candidate ships three measurable changes against v0.11.4 stable: (1) end-to-end throughput on the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark lifts to 22,140 tokens per second against v0.11.4 stable's 19,355 baseline — a 14.4 percent improvement on the same 8x H200 SXM5 + 1500 concurrent request configuration; (2) the first-token-latency median on Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B FP8 drops to 0.142 seconds from the prior 0.181 second floor; and (3) prefill cache hit-rate on the workload lifts from 71.3 percent to 79.4 percent on the radix-prefix-tree-v2 path. Hugging Face's Wednesday-afternoon hosted-endpoint dashboard recorded that Together AI and Fireworks AI have already rotated 38 percent of their Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B serving footprint to v0.11.5-rc1 inside the first six hours, and the SGLang project's RadixArk maintainer Lianmin Zheng published a Wednesday note confirming SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9 will hold the dev-tag through the v0.11.5 rc1-to-stable bake window with parity benchmark numbers tracking inside a 1.0 percent throughput gap.

bullets.body: A fresh ArXiv submission by Stanford CRFM PhD candidate Aryaman Arora and DeepMind senior research scientist Aakanksha Chowdhery dropped on Wednesday morning Pacific time at arxiv.org/abs/2605.10142 titled 'Reservoir Routing: A Stateful Mixture-of-Experts Path for Long-Horizon Agentic Inference', proposing a router-state-bank primitive that caches expert-selection trajectories across multi-turn agentic conversations rather than recomputing routing at every token. The paper reports on a 145B-parameter MoE backbone (the open Qwen3 MoE 60B uplifted with the contributed Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port from the Unsloth v2026.5.26 release) that reservoir routing recovers 4.1 percent end-to-end SWE-Bench Verified score over the baseline expert-routing-per-token path on long horizon tool-use chains exceeding eight tool calls — landing the augmented backbone at 78.7 against the published 74.6 baseline — while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by 31.4 percent measured on an 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Simon Willison flagged the paper in a Wednesday afternoon note as the first credible reservoir-style routing primitive shipped against a contemporary frontier-class MoE backbone, and Hacker News surfaced two early independent reproductions on Lambda Labs rentals with throughput numbers landing inside 2.5 percent of the Stanford-DeepMind reference sheet.

bullets.body: Apptronik announced Wednesday morning that its Apollo Generation 2 humanoid platform has cleared the first ten-unit cohort deployment at Mercedes-Benz's Tuscaloosa, Alabama final-assembly plant, with the production-trial cohort now operating across body-shop material-handoff and door-line subassembly stations on a single-shift rotation. The Apptronik Wednesday press release states that the first ten Apollo Gen 2 units cleared a 120-hour continuous-operation pre-flight (Saturday through Wednesday) at the Tuscaloosa fixture, with zero mean-time-between-failure events recorded, before being released into the production-trial cohort at the start of the Wednesday day shift; Mercedes-Benz separately confirmed that an additional 14-unit second cohort has been wheeled into the Tuscaloosa commissioning bay for a June 10 first-activation target. The deployment compresses the prior April 22 Mercedes-Apptronik MoU's nine-month single-digit-cohort ramp curve into a six-week first-deployment window and lifts the humanoid-on-factory-floor cohort count to seven OEM-platform pairs (Tesla-Fremont, Stellantis-Detroit, BMW-Leipzig, BMW-Spartanburg, Volkswagen-Wolfsburg, Boston Dynamics Hyundai-Pyeongtaek, Apptronik-Mercedes-Tuscaloosa). Reuters reported that Wall Street's Wednesday-afternoon reaction lifted humanoid-pure-play valuation comps (Figure private secondary, Sanctuary AI private secondary, Unitree H1 private secondary) by a weighted 4.7 percent on the deployment-cadence proof.
